# KnownGate

> A verification layer for food. It rules on what it is handed, shows its sources and their dates, and says so plainly when nobody knows.

KnownGate answers one question: does this food conflict with this premise?

A premise has two parts — send either, or both, in the same call:
- `restrictions` — what must not be present (FDA-9 keys plus any other name)
- `thresholds` — what must stay under, or over, a number (per serving, unit and basis explicit)

## Public pages

- [Evidence standard](https://knowngate.vercel.app/standard): what counts as proof
- [Question library](https://knowngate.vercel.app/questions): every question the gate can ask
- [Refusal rate](https://knowngate.vercel.app/refusals): how often we decline, with corpus measurements
- [Agents](https://knowngate.vercel.app/agents): WebMCP, MCP, and REST — same engine
- [Developers](https://knowngate.vercel.app/developers): tools, docs, and keys

## Check

- Human and agent workspace: https://knowngate.vercel.app/check
- WebMCP tools register on the page when a model context is present

## API (same-origin)

- `POST /api/knowngate/v0/check/item` — rule one subject against a premise
- `POST /api/knowngate/v0/check/place` — rule a venue chart against a premise
- `GET /api/knowngate/v0/label/{gtin}` — label findings for a GTIN
- `POST /api/knowngate/v0/freeze` — freeze a dated record to share

## Verdicts

- `no_conflict` / prose: no conflict found
- `conflict` / prose: conflict found
- `ask_one_question`
- `cannot_verify` / prose: couldn't verify

The word "safe" is never used in product copy.

## Optional

- Free-tier call budget `{N}` is undecided and must not be hardcoded
